alignments.note: Finite verb with its supplied object pronoun, a rule 7 helper on the verb English requires it for (rule 74's object clause).
Article emptied because the genitive rendered with the English possessive apostles' already occupies the determiner slot (rule 20).
Article to the, determining the possessor phrase.
Genitive noun rendered as the English possessor.
Finite verb rendered distribution was made; head on the noun carrying the διαδιδ- sense, was made being the empty support (rules 17, 91).
Dative adjective with its case preposition unto (rule 21).
Conjunction taking the lexical word of the English clause-introducer, according; the generalizing particle beside it takes the second word (rules 40, 50).

Generalizing ἄν aligned to the as of according as. Rule 50 holds that ἄν is aligned and that leaving it unrepresented is the recurring failure, and its spelled-out precedent ἃ … ἂν … ποιῇ → what things soever gives the relative its own word and the extra word to ἄν alone; this is that split for a conjunction. The competing reading keeps according as whole on καθότι and leaves ἄν empty, which rule 50 names as the failure and reports as a genuine correction.
Indefinite pronoun with its supplied generic completion one, headed on the indefinite (rule 17).
Finite verb had; the ASV spells both elements of the ἔχω + noun pair out, so rule 2 splits them (rule 73's contrast).

review_notes: Corrected καθότι ἄν: the accepted alignment kept according as whole on καθότι and left ἄν unrepresented, citing rule 61's ban on splitting a clause-introducer. That ban is scoped to a preposition governing an articular infinitive and to the archaic that of before that, and does not reach a particle standing beside a conjunction. Rule 50 governs ἄν directly, calls an unrepresented ἄν the recurring failure, and is the one place the contract says the disagreement report is itself a correction.

The reading now follows rule 50's spelled-out precedent: the conjunction keeps its lexical word according and the particle takes as. The competing reading — that rule 82's evidence of καθώς → according as as one conjunction's whole English carries over to καθότι — is named in the unit's note.
τοὺς πόδας τῶν ἀποστόλων is unchanged: the article is unrepresented under rule 20 because the genitive rendered as the English possessor occupies the determiner slot, exactly as at 4:37.
